builder_plan.scenario: You already need task-specific training and want to reduce its memory or compute cost.
builder_plan.change: Change only the training technique on a small controlled run after checking prerequisites.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current training recipe with the same model, data split, and evaluation.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Held-out quality, peak memory, training time, and full compute cost to the target quality.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Hypnos: A Dual-Phase End-to-End Platform for Scalable Continual Learning at the Edge
summary: Hypnos replaces always-on backpropagation-based continual learning (e.g., quantized latent replay) on edge devices with a dual-phase scheme: gradient-free prototype updates on a RISC-V MCU during operation and rehearsal-based gradient consolidation on a smart charger during idle periods. It requires custom hardware (ZCU104 FPGA, 28-nm synthesis), per-sample learning latency of roughly 8-10.5 seconds, and a platform split between MCU and charger that adds system complexity. It can fail if deployment conditions lack a reliable idle/charging phase for consolidation, if data streams do not match the CORe50-style continual-learning setting, or if the target hardware cannot host the required SoC design.
rationale: The method targets custom FPGA/RISC-V edge silicon for continual learning on sensor streams, which is outside the reader's GPU/API-based LLM production stack and cannot be adopted without dedicated hardware development.

claims.statement: Hypnos replaces always-on backpropagation-based continual learning (e.g., quantized latent replay) on edge devices with a dual-phase scheme: gradient-free prototype updates on a RISC-V MCU during operation and rehearsal-based gradient consolidation on a smart charger during idle periods. It requires custom hardware (ZCU104 FPGA, 28-nm synthesis), per-sample learning latency of roughly 8-10.5 seconds, and a platform split between MCU and charger that adds system complexity. It can fail if deployment conditions lack a reliable idle/charging phase for consolidation, if data streams do not match the CORe50-style continual-learning setting, or if the target hardware cannot host the required SoC design.

On CORe50 NICv2-391, Hypnos reports 78.6%-81.6% accuracy (state of the art for edge CL systems) with 3.8x fewer learning steps and 22x less learning compute than quantized latent replay at comparable latency (7.79s-10.54s per sample on-device).
